gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow's same-capacity DELTA 3 Max (2,048 Wh, $879) and DELTA 3 Ultra (3,072 Wh, $1,299) cannot be expanded, while only their Plus versions ($1,149 / $1,599) take the 2,048 Wh DELTA 3 Max Plus Smart Extra Battery (up to 10 / 11 kWh), and that the Smart Generator 3000's automatic start-stop works only with the DELTA 3, DELTA 3 Plus and DELTA 3 Ultra Plus (not the DELTA 3 Classic, DELTA 3 Max or DELTA 3 Ultra).
standout_why: I read solarkontor.de (rank 1, the only top result that opened and covers the whole lineup). It says only that 'The RIVER PRO and DELTA MAX & PRO can be expanded by adding an extra battery.' Those are older models. It has no extra-battery pairing for any DELTA 3 model and nothing on the Smart Generator, the alternator charger or exclusions. notebookcheck's RIVER 3 Plus piece covers only the RIVER 3 Plus EB300/EB600 (858 Wh max), with UK prices. tech.yahoo.com's DELTA 3 Plus review returned 403, trailandkale returned 404, and shopsolarkits returned 429, so none of those three could be checked. No page I could open separates Plus from non-Plus on expansion or generator auto-start.
decides: If the shopper may ever want more capacity or a whole-home setup with an auto-starting generator, the pick has to be a Plus model (DELTA 3 Plus, DELTA 3 Max Plus or DELTA 3 Ultra Plus). The cheaper DELTA 3 Max, DELTA 3 Ultra and DELTA 3 Classic look the same on the spec sheet, but they are fixed at their built-in capacity and are not on the Smart Generator auto start-stop list. That makes the $270 (Max to Max Plus) and $300 (Ultra to Ultra Plus) price gaps a choice about expansion, not about output alone. For a buyer who knows they will never expand, the non-Plus model is the cheaper route to the same capacity.
